Worldwide 22 species. Throughout Malesia except for Java and the Lesser Sunda Islands, in Malesia 11 species, 2 in Peninsular Malaysia.
Medium-sized to emergent tree, in peat swamp, heath forest, lowland to montane forest on a wide range of soil types, including limestone- and quartzite-derived soils.
Sumatra, Peninsular Malaysia and throughout Borneo. In Peninsular Malaysia, found in all states except Perlis, Melaka and Johor.

In Peninsular Malaysia, this species is found from 10--1200 m in lowland to lower montane forest, where it is common on mountain ridges. Formerly found in coastal padang formation on BRIS soil in Pak Kanchil F.R., Terengganu, but was burnt (Salleh Endut, pers. comm.). In Borneo, it grows to greater height and size, i.e., 55 m tall and 1 m diameter (Yii, 1995) and often forms pure stands in sandy heath forest over podzols (Whitmore, Trop. Rain For. Far East (1975) 172).
Endemic to Peninsular Malaysia; recorded only from G. Tahan, Pahang, and G. Rabong, Kelantan.

Restricted to lower and upper montane forest on quartzite-derived soils at 1200--2100 m altitude. Plants in shaded areas attain greater height and have greener leaves than those in exposed conditions, which have distinctly yellow foliage.

Three genera (Agathis, Araucaria Juss. and Wollemia W.G.Jones, K.D.Hill & J.M.Allen) with 41 species worldwide, largely in the southern hemisphere and concentrated in the Malesian region (13 species) and countries around the Pacific Ocean (Australia, New Zealand and S America). In Peninsular Malaysia represented by two species of Agathis.

In Peninsular Malaysia, medium-sized to emergent trees in lowland to upper montane forest; in peat swamp or on limestone, igneous or sedimentary rocks. Sometimes dominant and, in Borneo, sometimes forming pure stands. All species are wind-pollinated and their winged seeds wind-dispersed. Leaves are produced in flushes.
